Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Fear 12:21: And in the Midrash (Devarim Rabbah 9:3) they explained the verse (Ecclesiastes 8:8), "no man has power over the spirit, to restrain the spirit," concerning the matter of death; in these words: Rabbi Yehuda said, no man has power over the Angel of Death, to withhold him from himself; and "ruach" [spirit/wind] refers only to an angel, as it is said (Psalms 104:4), "He makes His angels winds [ruchot]." Rabbi Shimon ben Chalafta said: no man can make a weapon and be saved from the Angel of Death, along the lines of what is said, "He made shields for the wind" - and there is no dominion on the day of death; a person has no power to say, wait for me until I settle my accounts and until I instruct my household, and afterward I will come - therefore it is said, "and there is no dominion on the day of death" - to this point.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Fear 12:22: And Rabbi Abba himself further explains (Zohar, Vayakhel 199a) further particulars concerning the matters of death: he likened it to the story of the prophet Jonah, who was in a ship and was cast into the sea - like the soul, which, while in the body in this world, and after its departure the body is cast into the grave, and the grave is the fish that swallowed Jonah. And he said, of blessed memory: Jonah, who went down into the ship - this is the soul of a person, which descends into this world to be in a person's body. Why is it called Jonah [yonah, related to "wronging," ona'ah]? Because once it partners with the body, it is then "wronged" in this world, as it is said (Leviticus 25:17), "and you shall not wrong [tonu] one another." And then a person goes about in this world like a ship on the great sea, which is thought to be broken, as it is said (Jonah 1:4), "and the ship was thought to be broken."
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Fear 12:23: And when a person, while in this world, sins, and thinks he has fled from before his Master and pays no heed in this world, then the Holy One, blessed be He, casts a mighty stormy wind - this is the decree of judgment that always stands before the Holy One, blessed be He, and seeks judgment against the person from before Him. And this is what storms the ship and recalls the person's sins in order to seize him; once the person is seized by that storm, [falling] into his sickbed, what is written (Jonah 1:5)? "And Jonah went down into the innermost parts of the ship and lay down and fell fast asleep" - even though the person is in his sickbed, his soul does not awaken to return before his Master to release himself from his sins. What is written (ibid.)? "And the captain approached him" - who is the captain? This is the good inclination, which guides everything - "and said to him, why are you sleeping? Arise, call upon your God," and so on - this is not the time to sleep, for they are bringing you up for judgment for everything you did in this world; return from your sin, consider these words and return to your Master. "What is your occupation" - that you were engaged in, in this world, and confess it before your Master. "And from where do you come" - consider from where you came, from a putrid drop, and do not be haughty before Him. "What is your land" - consider that you were created from the earth and will return to the earth. "And of what people are you" - consider whether you have the merit of the fathers to shield you.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Fear 12:24: Once they bring him up for the supernal judgment, that storm, which is the decree of judgment storming against the person, demands of the King to judge those seized by the King, and they all come, one by one, before Him. At that hour the court convenes; some of them open in his merit, and some of them open in his guilt, and the decree of judgment demands judgment; and if that person is not meritorious, what is written (ibid. 1:13)? "And the men rowed hard to bring the ship back to dry land, but they could not" - those who argue in his merit strive to return him to this world and cannot. Why? "For the sea grew more and more stormy against them" - the decree of judgment goes and storms against the person's sins and overpowers them.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Fear 12:25: Then three appointed agents descend upon him: one who has recorded all the merits and all the sins the person did in this world; one who reckons his days; and one who went with him from when he was in his mother's womb. And behold, we have established that the decree of judgment does not settle until that time of which it is written (ibid. 1:15), "and they took up Jonah" - "and they took him up" - when they take him from his house to the house of graves, then they proclaim about him: if he is righteous, they proclaim about him and say, give honor to the image of the King; peace shall come, they shall rest on their couches, he who walked uprightly (Isaiah 57:2). From where do we derive this? As it is written (ibid. 58:8), "and your righteousness shall go before you, the glory of the LORD shall gather you." And if he is wicked, they proclaim about him and say, woe to so-and-so, better for him had he not been created. Then what is written (Jonah 1:15)? "And they cast him into the sea, and the sea ceased from its raging" - when they bring him into the house of graves, which is the place of judgment, then the decree of judgment that was storming settles from its rage.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Fear 12:26: And the fish that swallowed him - this is the grave. What is written (ibid. 2:1)? "And Jonah was in the belly of the fish" - the fish's innards, this is the belly of Sheol; from where do we derive this? As it is written (ibid. 2:3), "out of the belly of Sheol I cried," and he was in the fish's innards and called it the belly of Sheol. "Three days and three nights" - these are the three days a person is in the grave and his innards burst; after three days, that filth [the decomposing body] turns upon its face and says to it, take what you gave into me - you ate and drank every day and did not give to the poor, and all your days were like festivals and holidays while the poor were hungry, not eating with you - take what you gave into me. This is (Malachi 2:3), "and I will spread dung upon your faces," and so on - and we have established this [elsewhere].
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Fear 12:27: After that, from the third day onward, the person is judged through his eyes, his hands, and his feet, and it has been established that up to thirty days, all those thirty days the soul and the body are judged together, and therefore the soul remains below in the earth, not ascending to its place, like a woman who sits outside during all her days of impurity. Afterward the soul ascends and the body decays in the earth, until that time when the Holy One, blessed be He, will be aroused to revive the dead, and a voice is destined to be aroused in the house of graves and say (Isaiah 26:19), "awake and sing, you who dwell in the dust, for your dew is like the dew of lights, and the earth shall cast forth the shades" - to the extent relevant here.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Fear 12:28: And in the Tikkunim (53b) they likened the matter of Jonah in the ship in a different manner, but in any case, concerning the verse "arise, call upon your God," it agrees with the words of the Zohar. In these words: "arise, call upon your God" - this is the supernal Shechinah, which longs for you, and return to her, to your Master, who is the Holy One, blessed be He. Consider that an evil maidservant rules over you - this is the putrid drop - and of this it is said (Job 1:7), "and the LORD said to Satan, from where do you come?" - for all sins come from the limbs of the putrid drop, for in the Garden [Eden] it was said to the wicked, know from where you came, from a putrid drop. "And the men rowed hard to bring [the ship] back to dry land" - in repentance - "but they could not," for "the sea" - which is the decree of judgment - "grew more and more stormy against them" - to this point.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Fear 12:29: Further, concerning the matters of departure and the reckoning, I found in a manuscript "Margenita" of Rabbi Meir, peace be upon him, speaking of this; in these words: the Holy One, blessed be He, said to Israel: neither sufferings, nor rebukes, nor warning, nor promise, nor being cast about, nor length of days, nor patience, nor an agent, nor a command, nor curses, nor bans, nor consolations, nor shame, nor fear, nor dread of the World to Come, nor dread of the reckoning, nor dread of the judgment of Gehinnom, nor My name being profaned among the nations through you, will avail you. And whoever has all these deeds loses his merit and is withheld from him many good things, and his years are shortened, and he acquires a bad name, and his deeds and the sins of his fathers are remembered against him, and his prayer is despised in this world and the World to Come, and all his deeds are publicized and he gives judgment and reckoning for them, and every joy he rejoiced in through his inclination becomes mourning for him, and they are demanded from him with strange judgments and much shame, and cruel angels in a long world [an extended process]. Therefore it is said (Isaiah 10:3), "and what will you do on the day of visitation," and so on, "and where will you leave your glory?"
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Fear 12:30: Further, one who sins with his eyes, his eyes dim; one who sins with his ears, hears his own disgrace; one who sins with his mouth, his words are not heeded; one who sins in counsel, his livelihood diminishes; one who sins in thought, the radiance of his face changes; one who sins with his tongue, sufferings come upon him; one who sins with his hand, descends from his honor; one who sins with his heart, dies from worry; one who sins with his feet, his years are shortened; one who sins with his inclination, his inclination accuses him; one who sins and causes others to sin, buries his wife and his children and his household; one who sins through mockery, his sentence is sealed.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Fear 12:31: And what pleasure is there for a person, whose end is to depart from world to world - from life to death, from light to darkness, from sweet sleep to cramped and bitter sleep, from a sweet bed to the worm and the maggot, from sweet delicacies to the taste of dust, from a fine embrace to an embrace of dust? How many rich men left the world dejected! How many wise men had their wisdom become a stumbling block to them! How many mighty men had their might become a stumbling block to them! How many who raised children did not rejoice in their children! How many beautiful people had their beauty become a stumbling block to them! How many elders did not see honor! How many young men were cut down at their wedding canopy!
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Fear 12:32: And what pleasure is there in eating food that brings a person to many judgments; in joy that brings a person to many worries; in clothing that causes many mishaps; in fantasy that causes many pains; in sweet sleep that causes a strange death; in sin that loses many merits; in complaint that deprives many livelihoods?
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Fear 12:33: Who is destined for the World to Come? One who distances himself from transgressions, from fantasy, from mockery, from evil speech, and from ugliness and the like, and who fulfills the commandments and has performed a commandment in its true form, and who distances himself from sin and from mere recitation of prayer [without intent], and confesses his sins before the Holy One, blessed be He, and repents.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Fear 12:34: And one who associates with a wicked person banishes himself from this world and from the World to Come; and one who shows a pleasant face to a wicked person is among those who anger God; and one who deals deceitfully in his ways mourns in his end; and one who turns his fellow from a good way to an evil way dies in the midst of his days; and one who mocks the commandments, no mercy is shown him from Heaven; and one who mocks the poverty of the poor - in the end he toils and others eat his toil; and whoever habitually causes his fellow's face to redden [with shame], his ledger is opened against him that very day; and there is nothing harder than one who occupies himself with idle words.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Fear 12:35: Woe to one whom the world deceives; woe to one for whom the hour smiles [favorably, deceptively]; woe to one whose defender becomes his accuser; woe to one whose inclination overcomes him; woe to one against whom the wheel [of fortune] has turned; woe to one who loses his labor.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Fear 12:36: There is punishment that comes immediately and punishment that comes after a time; there is one after another, and there is all of them at once; there are some that come upon a person while he is awake, and some that come while he is asleep; there are some that are heavy and some that are like a fleeting breath; there is some with his knowledge and some without his knowledge; there is some in his old age and some in his youth; there is some in secret and some in the open; there is some at home and some while lodging away. Every trouble and distress, and jealousy, and breach, and mishap, diminish [the effect of] the sin.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Fear 12:37: There is one who serves the Omnipresent out of fear, so that his livelihood not be curtailed; and there is one out of love; and there is one out of shame; and there is one out of simplicity; and there is one in order to be seen; and there is one with the joy of rejoicing that the commandment should be performed through him; and there is one out of suffering, as it is said (Hosea 5:15), "in their distress they will seek Me" - and each one according to his deeds.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Fear 12:38: At the hour a person departs, the angel appointed over judgment stands opposite him and says to him: woe to this body that left the world empty of merits and full of sins. He looks at his feet and says: woe to the feet that did not walk uprightly; woe to the hands that occupied themselves with falsehood; woe to the innards that enjoyed theft; woe to the eyes that did not walk in faithfulness; woe to the ears that did not accept rebuke; woe to the mouth that did not occupy itself with Torah; woe to the flesh that did not toil in fear; woe to the inclination that did not submit before its Creator; woe to the heart that did not serve its Creator, for it is destined to stand in disgrace.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Fear 12:39: And he says to him: stand in judgment and recognize your deeds, and know from where you came and before whom you are destined to give judgment; and if you cannot answer, who can answer? And who can bear his sins, which are like fire to a garment, like a sword to the neck, like an arrow to the heart, like fetters to the feet, like darkness to the eyes, like gall to the mouth, like a pit to the foot, like [poor] plowing to the ears [an obscure/difficult reading], like a stumbling-block to strength, like evil days to old age, like sufferings to the body, like a severing to the horn, like gall to death, like a transgression to the Day of Judgment.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Fear 12:40: There is one who dies in the midst of his days, and there is one who departs from the world in innocence. Happy is one whose fear [of God] is upon his face; happy is one who is guarded from his sin; happy is one who is humble; happy is one whom the multitudes praise; happy is one who is lowly in his own eyes; happy is one who inclines his ear to hear the words of Torah; happy is one who hears the words of Torah every day. The Torah of the LORD is perfect, standing before a person while he occupies himself with his study, and it says: the LORD is with you, mighty warrior; behold, I have come to teach you, therefore I have gone out to meet you, to seek you early and find you. Happy are you if you remember me; happy are you if you hide me in your heart; happy are you if you uphold me; happy are you if you proclaim me; and every day my desires will be upon you, for through me your days shall increase. Distance yourself from transgression, and cleave to Torah, and flee from [seeking] authority, and be always in wisdom, and call upon your God always, for He will settle you and satisfy you and give you rest. And remember that you are a putrid drop, destined for dust and the pit; therefore distance yourself from repose and serve your God with joy, and it shall be for your compassion, for the way is bent low, and it shall become for you a lofty burden and provision. If you do this thing, He will make you shine like radiant lights and God will command for you, for if you serve your God with love and affection, happy are you in this world, and it shall be well for you in the World to Come - to this point I have found.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Fear 12:41: Further, Rabbeinu Tam wrote similar things in the Sefer HaYashar (Gate 17); he wrote that a person should say to his heart: my heart, my heart, do you not know that you were created only to return to dust? From the day of your existence, why have you not remembered your end? Do you not know that all the days you live on the earth are like a fleeting shadow, like chaff driven from the threshing floor, and like smoke from a chimney - your days are decreed and your life is cut short, and every day or night that passes over you, you are diminished by a portion of the portions of your life, and every day you draw nearer to the grave and fly away without a limb. And why have you not remembered that you are dust, and did you not know that you were formed from the earth? And in whom did you trust that you rebelled? And why are you hasty and do not reflect in your heart upon the bitter day - the day your counsel will be lost and your wisdom will spoil, the day your tongue will cleave to your palate, the day they will carry you on their shoulders, bear you, and cast you upon the lowest earth, and reckon you for every deed, and crush you like dust, and your fire shall not be quenched; the day you will see the reckoning arrayed and the book opened, and the scales of judgment and the cup of poison in the hand of the LORD - there its dregs shall be drained, and your soul shall moan at its bitterness. And what will you answer for your willful sins? For then you will see the fruit of your deeds and find your recompense.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Fear 12:42: And if you were to die like the death of an animal and not be destined to give a reckoning, you would have had reason to rejoice at your death; but you will go to a place more bitter than death, to a place of gloom, a land of darkness and the shadow of death - there dread will fall upon you and shame will cover you, and your garment will be a clod of maggots, and sulfur will be scattered upon your body, leaving you no remnant. Is not that day terrible and awesome - a day for which there is no ransom, a day of bitter weeping, mourning and lamentation, a day of trembling and outcry, a day of ruin and groaning, a day of bitter wailing, a day you will hold mourning, watch after watch, a day the wrath of God and His jealousy will burn and His fury will pour out like fire, a day sorrows and pains will multiply, a day every man will moan and clap his hands upon his loins, a day all his desires will perish, a day the soul will depart and the body will remain like a vessel full of shame, cast aside like a silent stone.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Fear 12:43: And now, son of man, to whom will you flee for help, or who will be your shelter? Will you not then say, woe is me, what have I done, why have I despised the word of the LORD and followed the stubbornness of my heart, and with what shall I cover myself, for I am naked? Gather yourself and be ashamed and humiliated over your sins, and give thanks to your God while your soul is still in your body and before the stars of your twilight darken; return one day before your death; hold fast to discipline, do not let it go, for it is your life - to this point.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Fear 12:44: And we find that even Rabban Yochanan ben Zakkai was anxious and afraid of the judgments of the World to Come, as they said (Berachot 28b): when Rabban Yochanan ben Zakkai fell ill, his disciples came in to visit him. When he saw them, he began to weep. His disciples said to him: our master, lamp of Israel, right-hand pillar, mighty hammer, why are you weeping? He said to them: were I being led before a king of flesh and blood, who is here today and in the grave tomorrow, whose anger against me, if he is angry, is not eternal anger, and whose imprisonment of me, if he imprisons me, is not eternal imprisonment, and whose putting me to death, if he puts me to death, is not eternal death, and whom I could appease with words and bribe with money - even so I would weep. Now that I am being led before the King of kings of kings, the Holy One, blessed be He, who lives and endures forever and ever, whose anger against me, if He is angry, is eternal anger, and whose imprisonment of me, if He imprisons me, is eternal imprisonment, and whose putting me to death, if He puts me to death, is eternal death, and whom I cannot appease with words nor bribe with money - and not only that, but there are two paths before me, one of the Garden of Eden and one of Gehinnom, and I do not know on which of them I am being led - shall I not weep? - to the extent relevant here.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Fear 12:45: And the Rosh, of blessed memory, wrote (Orchot Chaim, for Monday) in these words: "and your bed shall be drenched with tears, and your thoughts shall alarm you whenever you recall the dread of Rabban Yochanan ben Zakkai at the hour of his departure."
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Fear 12:46: And they said (Masechet Soferim, chapter 16, halachah 8), concerning the virtue of Rabban Yochanan ben Zakkai, of blessed memory: they said of Rabban Yochanan ben Zakkai that he did not leave a single passage of the Torah that he did not study; he studied Scripture, Targum, Midrash, halachot, aggadot, and parables - he studied everything. And so they said of him, that he said: were all the heavens parchment, and all the trees quills, and all the sea ink, it would not suffice to write the wisdom I learned from my teacher, and I have drawn from the wisdom of the sages only as a fly that dips into the great sea and diminishes it by something [infinitesimal] - to this point.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Fear 12:47: And our Rabbis, of blessed memory (Sukkah 28a), added further concerning the things he studied; they said of Rabban Yochanan ben Zakkai that he did not leave [unstudied] Scripture, Mishnah, halachot and aggadot, the fine points of the Torah, the fine points of the scribes, the leniencies and stringencies, gezeirah shavah [verbal analogy], calendrical calculations, gematriot, the speech of the ministering angels and the speech of demons and the speech of palm trees, the parables of launderers, the parables of foxes, a great matter and a small matter - the great matter, the Account of the Chariot; the small matter, the discussions of Abaye and Rava - to fulfill what is said (Proverbs 8:21), "to cause those who love me to inherit substance, and I will fill their treasuries" - to this point.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Fear 12:48: Further, I found chapters from the words of our Rabbis, of blessed memory, speaking of the matter of the beating of the grave [chibbut ha-kever]; I have seen fit to copy them here to arouse the heart to fear:
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Fear 12:51: How does a person die? Ministering angels come upon him - one of the ministering angels, and one of the angels of death, and one a scribe, and one who is appointed with him - and he says to him: arise, your end has come. He says to them: my end has not yet come. Immediately he opens his eyes and sees an angel whose length is from one end of the world to the other, from the sole of his foot to the crown of his head, full of eyes; his garment is fire, his covering is fire, all of him is fire, and a knife is in his hand, and a drop of gall hangs from it - from it he dies, from it he decomposes, from it his face turns green. And he does not die until he sees the Holy One, blessed be He, Himself, as it is said (Exodus 33:20), "for man shall not see Me and live" - in their lives they do not see, but they see at their death, as it is said (Psalms 22:30), "before Him shall all who descend to the dust bow down," and so on. Immediately he testifies against himself concerning everything he did in this world, and he testifies and the Holy One, blessed be He, seals it. If he is righteous, he hands over his soul to its Owner willingly; if he is completely wicked, he stiffens his neck and strengthens his inclination. From here our Rabbis, of blessed memory, said: even at the departure of a wicked person, his inclination overpowers him.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Fear 12:52: Rabbi Eliezer ben Yaakov says: just as he stiffens his neck in this world, so it is made hard for him at the hour of his departure, when he stands in judgment, as it is said (Psalms 112:10), "the wicked man shall see it and be angered," and so on. And at the hour of a righteous man's departure, what does it say? (Isaiah 57:1), "the righteous man perishes," and so on. And at the hour of a wicked man's departure, what does it say? (II Samuel 23:6), "but the wicked shall be all of them as thorns," and so on.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Fear 12:54: They asked Rabbi Elazar: what is the judgment of the grave? He said to them: when a person departs from the world, the Angel of Death comes and sits on his grave and strikes him with his hand and says to him: arise, tell me your name. He says to him: it is revealed and known before Him who spoke and the world came into being that I do not know what my name is. Immediately he inserts spirit and soul into his body and stands him up and obligates him in judgment.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Fear 12:55: Rabbi Yehoshua ben Levi said: half fire and iron chains are in his hand. Once, his limbs are pulled apart; a second time, his bones are pulled apart, and ministering angels come and gather them and stand him up, and strike him a third time, and demand judgment of him, and judge him measure for measure. On the first day and the second day they judge him thus. On the third day they judge him with blows: they strike him on his two eyes, because he did not see [what he should] and yet claimed [to have seen]; and on his ears, because he did not hear and yet claimed [to have heard]; and on his lips, because he brought forth vain words from his lips; and on his tongue, because it testified false testimony; and on his feet, because his feet hastened toward transgression. From here our Rabbis, of blessed memory, said: whoever hastens his feet toward transgression, the Angel of Death hastens toward him; and whoever speaks evil-speech, slandering his fellow, his death is by croup [quinsy].
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Fear 12:57: Rabbi Meir said in the name of Rabbi Elazar: harder is the day of judgment that the Holy One, blessed be He, judges a person in the grave than the judgment of Gehinnom. The judgment of Gehinnom applies from twenty years of age and up, but the judgment of the grave - even the righteous are judged by it; even nursing infants, even suckling babes, are judged by it. But our Rabbis, of blessed memory, said: one who dwells in the Land of Israel and dies on the eve of Shabbat does not see the judgment of the grave. And what should a person do to be saved from the judgment of the grave? Let him be a lover of acts of righteousness and a lover of rebukes and a lover of acts of loving-kindness, and let him bring guests into his house, and let him pray his prayer with intention - even if he dies outside the Land, he will not see it, as it is said (Jonah 2:3), "and he said, I called out of my distress," and so on.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Fear 12:58: Ben Azzai says: there are three judgments, and each is harder than the other, and all three are before the Holy One, blessed be He. Rabbi Akiva says: are all three really before the Holy One, blessed be He? Is it not that the judgment of the grave is judged by itself, and the judgment of Gehinnom alone is judged by itself, and the judgment of Heaven alone is before the Holy One, blessed be He - if there is no judgment against him, they release him immediately, and if not, they judge him a lengthy judgment.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Fear 12:60: Rabbi Yosi said: come and see how great is the difference between an animal and a person. An animal - however much suffering it bears in the world, they slaughter it and flay it and there is no judgment against it. But a person - however much suffering he bears in this world, after his death, if he is completely righteous, they release him from judgment; and if he is completely wicked, they judge him with severe judgments.
